plugins.name: git-steward
plugins.description: Multi-repo git stewardship: branch pruning, commit & history hygiene, secret/large-file removal, repo health, work-item triage, branch and MR sizing, and CI pipeline health — plus a fleet-wide CI watchdog that monitors every pipeline in every repo and autofixes failures (gated by default, autonomous per policy). Analyze (read-only) and apply (mutating) modes stack from a single operation to a single repo to the whole fleet.

plugins.name: ui-ux-studio
plugins.description: UI/UX design studio: a director skill that orchestrates real-world-inspired UI work — deciding when to design from rules, when to pull concrete references, and when the reference library is too thin and must be grown by discovering + extracting new sites; its variations mode builds the same brief as N style-skill-driven variants (one taste skill per variant, built in isolation) with a compare page. Bundles the ui-ux-references example library, a ui-ux-gallery skill to browse it in the browser, a style-tweaker skill that injects a live dev-only sidebar for tweaking design tokens (fonts, colors, spacing, per-component knobs) in the running app with A/B snapshots and CSS export, a ui-adversary skill that spawns an adversarial agent to critique a live web UI with evidence-backed, severity-ranked findings (screenshots, GIFs, a11y tree, console/network, contrast and tap-target probes), and composes with the ui-ux-pro-max rules skill.

plugins.name: ui-ux-pro-max
plugins.description: UI/UX design intelligence: styles, color palettes, font pairings, product-type guidance, UX guidelines, and charts across many stacks. Open-source skill by nextlevelbuilder (MIT), vendored into this marketplace at upstream sha b7e3af8 (v2.5.0) — see the plugin's VENDORED.md to take a new upstream release.

plugins.name: prospector
plugins.description: Lead-generation system for a web-redesign business: gather companies within a defined scope, store rich dossiers (sector, revenue, employees), capture + taste-audit their websites, score the money×bad-site×site-matters opportunity, deep-capture committed redesigns into a full blueprint (multi-page screenshots + code + issue register + implementation plan), and run an outreach workspace (agent-drafted email + copy-paste text → validate the contact → send). Runs locally as a dashboard over a filesystem store, or hosted in a container with shared-password auth; a headless claude agent-runner drains hunt/deep-dive/outreach/blueprint (cloud API), or a local Claude session can drain it off your subscription via the prospect-worker skill. Import/export the whole store as a bundle.

plugins.name: llm-mode
plugins.description: Working-discipline modes distilled from top Claude models, written down so any session can run them. Ships the fable-mode skill — Fable 5's five-gate task loop (scope, evidence, adversarial reasoning, verification, calibrated reporting) plus standing habits — to make planning, debugging, and review noticeably more rigorous on Opus 4.8 or Sonnet 5.

plugins.name: project-genesis
plugins.description: AI-native project bootstrapping: interview → foundation docs → minimal scaffold + CI. Generates a CLAUDE.md agent contract with a doc map and enforceable maintenance rules, plus lean product/features/architecture/decisions/conventions docs designed for future LLM sessions (current-state only, explicit non-goals and restrictions, a feature ledger with resume pointers, read-before-touching pointers). Stack-agnostic — asks or detects the stack and adapts.

plugins.name: skill-smith
plugins.description: Meta-tooling for developing and refining Claude Code skills. Ships skill-author: create new skills or audit/restructure existing ones against a written authoring standard — discoverable descriptions in the user's own trigger words, skimmable numbered structure, human-readable prose, bounded loops, correct plugin/marketplace wiring ('create a skill', 'audit this skill', 'make this skill readable'). And skill-retro: a session retrospective that reviews the skills and plugins used in the current session, grades their perceived performance with session evidence, appends findings to each skill's append-only FEEDBACK.md, and proposes concrete user-approved SKILL.md edits — the feedback loop that makes skills improve from real usage ('skill retro', 'review this session', 'how did the skills perform').

plugins.name: scroll-world
plugins.description: Build an immersive scroll-scrubbed 'fly through the world' landing page for any industry or brand using Higgsfield: cohesive isometric diorama scenes and seamless camera flights driven by scroll position (Apple-style scrubbing), with a portable framework-agnostic scrub engine for plain HTML, Next.js, Vue, or a Python-served page. Fork of oso95/scroll-world (MIT) vendored at upstream f941ef9 (v0.2.0) — see the plugin's VENDORED.md; local divergence expected.

plugins.name: writing-craft
plugins.description: Writing skills for making technical work readable. Ships plain-report — turn a technical analysis, run, or dataset into a report a reader with zero context and no technical knowledge can follow: concepts defined before use, internal codes renamed to human labels, every claim backed by one concrete result, honest limits, a glossary that grows with reader questions, and an audit mode that flags readability defects without rewriting.

plugins.name: marketing-presentations
plugins.description: Build HTML presentations, decks, report pages, and story pages that feel like high-end marketing/landing pages — scroll-driven visual storytelling with award-site craft (oversized typography, choreographed motion, section-by-section narrative), written first as a visual script and then implemented as a single-file HTML page. Ships the marketing-presentations skill: build (content → visual script → page, self-scored against 8 dimensions in bounded passes) and extract <url> (grow the knowledge base from a reference site). Principles, 15 style axes with BRUTALIST/EDITORIAL/REPORT poles, and implementation patterns were validated in a design-extraction lab — three award-site extract → blind-clone → evaluate cycles, each passing at 8.3–8.6/10.

plugins.name: model-router
plugins.description: Quota-aware model routing for Claude Code: keeps the main session on a strong model and pushes mechanical work to cheaper tiers. Jev (TypeSafe's decision model) decides the tier of every Agent spawn in a PreToolUse hook and advises on prompts that are delegate work, failing open without a key. Ships the standing routing policy (injected at session start), Haiku/Sonnet worker agents (ci-watcher, sweeper, mechanic, reviewer, sysadmin), Sonnet-pinned status-report and ship skills, a per-machine setup, a shared Jev client any plugin can call for its own bounded, repeated, expensive-to-get-wrong decisions (with the skill that says when not to), and a bi-weekly per-workstation usage review that measures where the tokens went and what the decider did.

plugins.name: web-design-guides
plugins.description: A web-designer agent (plan a site or page, audit a URL or code with severity-ranked findings, answer design questions) plus four lazily-loaded knowledge skills distilled from Lovable's public web-design guides: site architecture and navigation, marketing-page conversion, web UI foundations, and brand identity basics. Rules are paraphrased and source-tagged; each skill is a short rule set plus an index of per-guide notes read only when needed.

plugins.name: context-checkpoint
plugins.description: Deliberate context compaction for Claude Code: a UserPromptSubmit hook that reads the live context size from the session transcript and, every N% of the window, after a cold-cache pause, or on a task-boundary prompt, decides whether to keep or compact — on relevance and freshness of what is in context, not its size. A cheap model digests the transcript into five lines (in flight / closed / stale / poison / next needs) for the console, and TypeSafe's Jev decision model grades that digest with calibrated probabilities; the hook combines the grades by arithmetic, with a loss-risk veto. Falls back to asking the session's own model when no key or no answer. Ships the hook, a per-machine config, --status and --dry-run readings, and a skill explaining the criteria and the measurements.

plugins.name: code-maps
plugins.description: Maps of a codebase as navigable HTML pages, built from what the code compiles to and does rather than from reading it. Ships java-diagrams: class and package diagrams for a Java project, read from bytecode, cross-checked against jdeps, every view verified against the extracted graph and bounded so it stays readable. And execution-trace: a run trace that follows one execution from the command line to its last effect, step by step like a debugger, redrawn through layers (process, code, state, data, disk), with excerpts cut from the source at build time, call arrows read from bytecode and classes filtered by a measured class-load log.

plugins.name: log-craft
plugins.description: Readable, good-looking CI job logs. Ships ci-log-design: audit a GitLab CI job log with a scoring script, judge it against a written taste guide, redesign it with a small text-art vocabulary (title rules, folded steps, failure cards, duration bars, tables, a verdict line), and apply it through a shared POSIX-sh and Node logging library with a demo, a canary job and a renderer for before/after proof.

plugins.name: app-replicator
plugins.description: Replicate an existing web app from the outside: a product-teardown skill that studies a live app in the user's real Chrome through one extractor agent and writes an evidence-tagged replication spec a blind rebuilder can work from — surface map, feature inventory with tier gating, behaviour specs measured by probes (audio, timers, editors, state, persistence), API map, design tokens and an asset catalogue (copyrighted media catalogued, never downloaded) — shaped to seed project-genesis. Every claim is tagged measured / observed / documented / inferred / unverified and checked by a lint. Planned: replication-verify (blind-clone fidelity check).
